bull_bear.body: Deleveraging priority (Net debt down to INR 70cr); Partial divestment of Texas Lifesciences to focus on core biologicals; Dividend payout at all-time high; Working capital management to reduce receivables (currently INR 92cr).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Timing volatility in government tender rollouts (Animal Health); Raw material cost inflation due to supply chain disruptions; Regulatory changes requiring unplanned compliance capex; Political instability in African markets.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes 'operational discipline' and 'foundation strengthening'; Acknowledges tender delays as timing issues not demand issues; Confident in sustaining Poultry margins but wary of external forces.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Invoicing in Africa is split: USD for cross-border/export, local currency for domestic sales in operating countries; BSL-3 facility currently undergoing optimization for cost/efficiency rather than full immediate ramp; Petcare segment currently has zero commercial vaccine revenue despite rising pet population.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Poultry Healthcare: Q4 +41%, FY26 +21%, driven by deeper penetration and H9N2 license. Animal Healthcare: Impacted by tender timing delays, but Q4 execution improved. International: Focused on Africa (VITAL 2 program, USD invoicing) and stabilizing Nepal ops. Petcare: No commercial vaccines yet, long-term focus.

deepdive.thesis: Hester Biosciences delivered a sharp profitability inflection in Q4FY26 (PAT +174% standalone) driven by record Poultry Healthcare margins and mix, offsetting lingering Animal Healthcare tender delays. The commissioning of Fill-Finish and BSL-3 facilities positions the company for operating leverage in FY27, provided government tender execution normalizes and new avian influenza products gain traction.

open.item: Going forward priority is to strengthen and scale the core biologicals and vaccine business, expand domestic and export market penetration, improve product mix and capacity utilization, and maintain working-capital discipline.

After a ~30% YoY decline in Animal Health revenue in FY26 from tender delays, management expects to recover the Animal Healthcare business from Q1 FY27 onwards, with execution having started picking up in Q4.
Hester is working towards launching its own Lumpy Skin Disease vaccine in India, expected in the middle of the next financial year (FY27), after which government may shift from Goat Pox.
Management remains on track to achieve breakeven in Africa operations by FY28.
Management aims to sustain the highest-ever ~INR65cr quarterly poultry revenue with ~30s% margins as a base, though noting external forces make it hard to predict.
Management is aiming to return to an approximately 50:50 revenue mix between Poultry and Animal Healthcare (currently ~70:30 skewed to poultry) to avoid hyper-dependence on any single division.
Management is working to reduce the elevated receivables (~INR92cr, jumped due to >33% of sales occurring in Q4) and improve the number of receivable days.
Management stated focus to reduce the elevated bad-debt write-offs (~INR6.5cr in FY26 vs INR2.4cr prior year), expecting them not to remain so alarming going forward.

Management flagged external risks including volatility in tender business timing and rising raw material costs linked to global geopolitical developments and supply chain disruptions, to be managed via efficiency and calibrated price actions.
Hester is scouting how to enter African Swine Fever vaccine manufacturing (no vaccine currently exists globally) but has no visibility and no outer timeline.
Management affirmed the endeavor and confidence to reach the historical ~25% net margin level achieved 6-7 years ago.
Management indicated ~21% steady-state operating margins are sustainable and should be used as a base for the foreseeable future.
Management stated an internal determination to return to the historical ~33-34% EBITDA margins achieved in the vaccine-only era, though without a committed timeline.
Nepal plant full potential stated at Rs 50-80 crores depending on vaccine product mix.

verdicts.item: The expanded freeze-drying capacity at Hester India (capex already incurred) will more than double current capacity and commence operation in Q3 FY25.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 5Q past horizon Q3FY25

verdicts.item: Low pathogenic Avian Influenza (H9N2) vaccine is planned for launch in Q4 FY25 or possibly Q1 FY26.
verdicts.note: 'During the quarter, we also received both the marketing and manufacturing licenses for H9N2 Avian Influenza vaccine' - about a year past the original Q4 FY25/Q1 FY26 window.

verdicts.item: Once H9N2 is commercially available, Hester expects to register and supply the vaccine in quite a few countries; India market estimated at Rs 80-100 crores with a bigger world market.
verdicts.note: H9N2 licensed and 'Export opportunities will evolve differently across countries', but multi-country registration specifics and the India Rs 80-100cr market size not restated.

verdicts.item: Focus remains on growing the health-product and pet-care segments to equalize dependence on the vaccine-heavy range, leveraging the private distribution network.
verdicts.note: Health products (gut health/probiotics) introduced and Petcare scaling, with a stated aim to rebalance away from over-dependence on one division - equalization ongoing.

verdicts.item: Deferred PPR and Lumpy Skin Disease immunization programs (causing a 33% Animal Health decline) are deferrals not cancellations, with traction and a return expected in Q2 FY26 and beyond.
verdicts.note: Deferrals-not-cancellations thesis vindicated but late: 'the planning ... to happen from Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 sort of didn't really go through ... from Q4, it did start to pick up' - return came in Q4, not …

verdicts.item: Avian Influenza vaccine launch is pending only regulatory clearances, which are anticipated to come within this quarter (Q2 FY26).
verdicts.note: The 'within Q2 FY26' clearance did not occur; the H9N2 licenses were received only in Q4 FY26.

verdicts.item: Management is confident of returning to growth in the coming quarters of FY26 as institutional demand normalizes and Pet Care and Poultry momentum increases.
verdicts.note: Growth returned in Q4 (standalone +22%, Poultry +41%) and PPR execution improved, but full institutional normalization still pending ('recover it from this quarter onwards').

verdicts.item: Despite past expressed interest, management stated Hester is not into FMD vaccines and has no short-term plan to get into FMD.
verdicts.note: 'FMD is something which at the moment, we are yet discussing, but ... our priority is all other vaccines' - the not-into-FMD/no-near-term stance held.

verdicts.item: Given rising African demand, management will optimize capacity across the three plants (Nepal, India, Africa), with Nepal's PPR-focused capacity to be leveraged.
verdicts.note: India capacity expanded to serve export markets while Nepal is monitored for 'operational stability and long-term sustainability' - cross-plant optimization ongoing amid Nepal weakness.

verdicts.item: Management expects to receive government permission to repurpose the BSL-3 facility (from COVID antigen to animal vaccines) in the next few months, then expand animal vaccine product range.
verdicts.note: 'During the year, we capitalized our Fill-Finish as well as BSL-3 facilities' - government-permitted repurposing completed to capitalization.

verdicts.item: Management has taken up an objective to gain more market share in the poultry segment in the coming months to drive an upward trend irrespective of industry dynamics.
verdicts.note: 'growing by 41% in Q4 ... supported by deeper market penetration, expanded placements, stronger field execution' - poultry market-share/upward-trend objective delivered.

verdicts.item: The INR182 crore capital work in progress at the India plant is expected to be fully capitalized by March 2026, after which the plant will contribute meaningfully and enable a significant scale-up in vaccine production.
verdicts.note: 'During the year, we capitalized our Fill-Finish as well as BSL-3 facilities, as a part of our broader manufacturing and infrastructure expansion initiative.' [±10% rule]
